decision: Apple's own specification names Profile 5, Profile 10 and Profile 20 and never names Profile 7

result: this is an HLS delivery requirement, not a hardware capability statement; my claim that the hardware cannot compose dual layers is not supported by it and must be measured

decision: the dvcC on the enhancement track decodes to profile 7 level 6 with rpu 1, el 1, bl 0
why: reading the 32-byte payload 01000e3660... as the Dolby Vision configuration record gives version 1.0, profile 7, level 6, and bl_present 0, which says the base layer lives in the other track
result: confirms the file is genuinely Profile 7.6 dual track rather than mislabelled

decision: the enhancement layer is a residual signal, not a picture, so it cannot be composited by layering
why: signalstats over the EL track gives YLOW equal to YHIGH equal to 512 at t=30s and t=60s, meaning every pixel is exactly 10-bit mid-grey, while at t=10s it ranges 512 to 563; a layer that is uniformly mid-grey most of the time is a difference signal awaiting a per-frame polynomial reconstruction, not an image
evidence: ffmpeg signalstats over FEL_test_for_AVS.mp4 stream v:1
result: answers the two-stream question: there is nothing to overlay, and blending it would produce garbage

decision: our FFmpeg build can parse the Dolby Vision RPU but nothing in our stack can apply it
why: libPlaybackFFmpeg.a exports ff_dovi_attach_side_data, ff_dovi_configure and the dovi_rpu_* family, so the metadata is reachable, while applying it needs both layers decoded to pixel buffers, a 12-bit compositing step and display characteristics visionOS does not expose
result: the affordable move is to read the RPU and report the profile, not to reconstruct

decision: the unmet-capability model is binary, not three-tier
why: the owner corrected my fatal/degraded/silent split: degradation is what the player does, not a class of message, so the only distinction that changes the surface is whether playback happened at all

decision: the deck expansion sequence is content-out, grow, content-in

decision: this Vision Pro has a Dolby Vision decoder, measured
why: VTDecompressionSessionCreate for kCMVideoCodecType_DolbyVisionHEVC returns -12909 kVTVideoDecoderBadDataErr on a bare description, meaning the decoder was found and rejected the empty description, while all six ProRes types return -12906 kVTCouldNotFindVideoDecoderErr on the same kind of description
result: Dolby Vision is a capability we have; ProRes is not

decision: my first Dolby Vision assertion was the wrong bar and failed for a reason that carried no information
